title: Mlai entry domain gradient descent
question: In plain terms, how does gradient descent actually update a model's parameters during training?
idealAnswer:
The model computes a loss function measuring how wrong its predictions are, and gradient descent computes the gradient (partial derivatives) of that loss with respect to each parameter

The gradient points in the direction of steepest increase of the loss, so parameters are updated in the opposite direction to reduce the loss

The learning rate controls the step size of each update, too large and training can diverge or oscillate, too small and training is slow or gets stuck

Batch gradient descent uses the whole dataset per update, stochastic gradient descent uses one example at a time, and mini-batch gradient descent (the common practical choice) uses small batches, trading off stability and speed

This process repeats over many iterations or epochs until the loss converges to a minimum, or training is stopped
